content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The initial specification is ready for review:

- [Bookmark Manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

The checklist passes all 16 quality checks. The proposed v1 covers saving, editing, deleting, searching, tagging, favoriting, validation, duplicate warnings, persistence, responsive layouts, and keyboard accessibility.

Current scope assumes a private, single-user app without accounts, cloud sync, sharing, browser extensions, or bulk import/export.

Please approve the specification or describe any changes. I’ll wait for approval before creating the implementation plan or writing code.

Thanks for putting this together — I read through it and a lot of it matches what I had in mind: saving links, editing them, deleting with a confirm, searching, tagging, and it working on my phone and laptop. But there are a few things that are important to me that either aren't here or work differently than I'd expect, so I can't approve it yet.

A few things I want to raise:

1. **Typing in the title myself.** I saw the note that I'd have to enter the title and details by hand. That's not really what I pictured. When I paste in a link, I'd expect the app to go grab the page's title and a short description for me automatically — and ideally the little site icon and a preview picture too — so I mostly just paste and save. I still want to be able to fix or rewrite that title and description myself, both when saving and later, but the app doing the first pass is a big part of why I'd want this.

2. **Saving the same link twice.** Your version warns me but lets me keep a second copy on purpose. I'd actually rather it never make duplicates — if I try to save a link I've already got, just take me to the one I already saved so I can edit it. I don't want two of the same thing in my list.

3. **"Read later."** I often save things I haven't read yet. I'd like to mark a bookmark as unread/to-read, and be able to look at just those in one place, then mark it read when I'm done so it drops off that list.

4. **Archiving vs. deleting.** Delete should be the permanent "it's gone" action, yes. But I'd also like a gentler option — archive — to tuck a bookmark away so it's out of my normal list and searches but not actually destroyed, with its own place to look at archived ones and bring them back.

5. **Notes.** I'd like the notes to be able to hold more than a line — a proper note I can format a bit and have it show nicely when I look at the bookmark.

6. **Searching.** Plain text search is good, but I'd also want to search by tag directly (something like typing the tag), match an exact phrase when I put it in quotes, and combine conditions (this and that, or either one). And I'd like the tag box to suggest tags I've already used as I type.

7. **Sorting.** I don't only want newest-first — I'd like to choose how the list is ordered, like by title or by date.

Could you fold these in and show me a revised version? Happy to talk through any of them.

The revised specification now includes all seven requested changes:

- [Revised Bookmark Manager specification](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md)
- [Updated quality checklist](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/checklists/requirements.md)

The checklist passes all 16 checks with no unresolved clarification markers.

Please pay particular attention to these documented defaults:

- New bookmarks are not marked “To read” unless selected.
- Sorting supports title, date added, and date updated in both directions.
- Archived bookmarks remain excluded from normal searches.
- Similar URLs with different paths, queries, or fragments remain distinct.
- Phone and laptop layouts are supported, but cross-device synchronization remains out of scope.

If these choices and the revised behaviors look right, approve the specification and I’ll prepare the implementation plan next.

This looks great — you've captured everything I asked about, and the way you've spelled it out matches what I had in my head.

I read through the details you flagged and I'm happy with those choices:
- New bookmarks not being "To read" until I pick that — yes, that's what I'd want.
- Sorting by title, date added, and date updated both directions — perfect.
- Archived ones staying out of my normal searches — exactly.
- Links that only look similar but go to different pages staying separate — that's right; I only want the truly-same link to be treated as a duplicate.
- Phone and laptop working, with syncing across devices being a later thing — fine with me for now.

I especially like that pasting a link I already saved just takes me straight to the existing one instead of making a copy, that I can write a proper formatted note, and that the search shows me examples so I don't have to memorize anything.

The specification is approved. Please go ahead and prepare the implementation plan.

content:
The implementation plan is ready for approval:

- [Implementation plan](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md)
- [Research decisions](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/research.md)
- [Data model](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/data-model.md)
- [HTTP API contract](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/openapi.yaml)
- [Search grammar](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/contracts/search-grammar.ebnf)
- [Validation guide](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/quickstart.md)

The plan uses Node 24 LTS, React 19.3, Vite 8, Fastify 5, SQLite, and structured Tiptap notes, based on their current official support information: [Node releases](https://nodejs.org/en/about/previous-releases), [React versions](https://react.dev/versions), [Vite releases](https://vite.dev/releases), and [Fastify documentation](https://fastify.dev/docs/latest/).

Key design choices include:

- One deployable server and one SQLite database
- Database-enforced duplicate prevention
- SSRF-hardened metadata retrieval with locally stored processed images
- Validated structured notes instead of stored HTML
- A purpose-built Boolean search parser
- Responsive and keyboard-accessible interaction testing

There are no unresolved clarifications or constitution violations, and the OpenAPI contract validates successfully. No implementation tasks or code have been created yet.

Please approve the plan or request changes. Once approved, I’ll generate the dependency-ordered task breakdown.

That's a lot of technical detail I'll trust you on — the choice of tools and how it's built under the hood isn't something I can judge, and I'll leave those to you.

What matters to me is that the plan still delivers the things we agreed on, and from your summary it sounds like it does: pasting a link pulls in the page details, I can't end up with two copies of the same link, I can write proper formatted notes, the read-later and archive lists work, and the search understands phrases, tags, and the and/or stuff. One thing I'm glad to see mentioned is that you're being careful about safety when the app goes out to fetch a page's details — I hadn't thought about that, but it sounds sensible.

The plan is approved. Please go ahead and put together the task breakdown.

content:
The implementation task breakdown is ready:

- [Task breakdown](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/tasks.md)

It contains 92 dependency-ordered tasks:

- 32 shared setup, foundation, security, and release tasks
- 19 for saving links and preventing duplicates
- 14 for search, tags, filters, and sorting
- 7 for Read Later
- 11 for editing and formatted notes
- 9 for archive, restore, and deletion
- 55 tasks identified as safely parallelizable

Each user story has its own test-first phase and independent acceptance checkpoint. Every approved requirement and success criterion is mapped to implementation and verification work.

The suggested MVP is User Story 1: paste a link, retrieve its details safely, preserve manual changes, save it durably, and prevent duplicate links.

All tasks pass the required checklist format with sequential IDs, story labels, and exact file paths. No code has been implemented yet. Please approve the breakdown when you’re ready to begin implementation.

content:
Implementation is ready for review at **http://maker:4000**.

Delivered:

- Automatic metadata, icons, and previews with guarded fetching
- Strict duplicate prevention
- Search phrases, tags, Boolean expressions, filters, and sorting
- Read-later workflow
- Formatted notes and editing
- Archive, restore, and confirmed deletion
- Responsive desktop, phone, and 320px layouts
- Clean persistent SQLite database and production startup configuration

All 159 automated checks pass, including 14 browser journeys. Production readiness, accessibility scanning, clean startup, and database isolation were verified.

Artifacts:

- [README](/work/README.md)
- [Validation report](/work/specs/001-bookmark-manager/validation.md)
- [Application screenshot](/work/prototypes/bookmark-manager-final.png)

The approved Spec Kit implementation workflow drove the build and task tracking. The only outstanding release validation is the external 100-page metadata corpus; human screen-reader and independent usability studies are also documented as unavailable in this environment.

I spent some time actually clicking around and trying it out, and it does what we agreed on. Here's what I checked myself:

- Saving a link works, and when I tried to save the same link a second time it wouldn't make a copy — it told me it's already saved and pointed me to the one I had, even when I left off the trailing slash. That's exactly the no-duplicates behavior I wanted.
- Marking something "To read" put it in the To Read list, and I could find it there.
- Archiving a link took it out of my normal list and out of my searches, but I could still find it in the Archive and bring it back — and when I restored it, it kept its details and its read status.
- Search handled an exact phrase in quotes, finding by a tag, and combining things with "or".
- I could reorder the list by title and by date.

The page looks clean and matches what I pictured, and the empty state nicely tells a first-time person to save their first link.

I understand two things are noted as not fully checkable here — running the big batch of real web pages to confirm the auto-details, and a proper hands-on test with screen-reader users. I'm fine treating those as follow-up checks rather than blockers, since everything we actually agreed on is working in front of me.

This is what I asked for. I'm happy to accept it.
